title: Integrity monitoring for alt-PNT: solution-separation FDE, protection levels and a Stanford diagram
summary: A stdlib-only simulated UAV flight with INS, VIO-like velocity, intermittent visual-geolocalization fixes (repetitive-texture outliers, map-misregistration bias, dropouts over water), optional coarse MagNav-like fixes and a GNSS that is jammed and then spoofed. An 8-state EKF with chi-square innovation gating feeds a solution-separation bank that detects, excludes or (with only two sources) alerts and resolves by dead-reckoning consistency, computes horizontal protection levels against an alert limit, and reports MI/HMI, availability, time-to-alert and an ASCII/SVG Stanford diagram. A monitor-off negative control shows the misleading-information events the monitor removes. v2 (altpnt_v2.py, calibration.py) extracts measured error models from sibling samples (OpenVINS / KISS-ICP / nadir-VO heading and scale, real visual-geoloc availability, bias and residuals, TRN confidence-vs-error), adds heading and scale states, a DeCleene/Rife-style Gaussian overbound with a bias term, per-source fault priors and TRN measurement covariance from particle spread, and shows that v1's zero-MI result fails under measured models (MI* 0 => 8901 of 12000 epochs) while v2 restores zero MI at 13-26 % availability instead of 41.7 %.
verified: ran with python3.14.7 stdlib on 2026-11-06: default run, --magnav, --no-gnss, --al-sweep, 20-seed Monte Carlo for 8 configurations, CSV and SVG writers (SVG rendered with macOS qlmanage and inspected); 15 unit tests pass (python3 -m unittest), and the detection tests were confirmed to fail with detection disabled. Synthetic data only; no real flight log or indexed repo was run. v2: ran with python3.14.7 and 3.12.14 stdlib on 2026-11-06: calibration.py --check reproduces calibration.json from the committed sibling results; 20-seed Monte Carlo over 29 world/filter rows (182 s), v1 rows identical to the v1 table; 10 v2 unit tests pass. Error models are measured on short real runs (27-197 s) and replayed over a synthetic 600 s flight; correlation times and fault-rate priors for GNSS are assumptions.
